subject: Dedicated capacity SLA: tokens/sec & latency measurement methodology
messages:
From: Nina Torres <nina@cloudscale.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing/SLAs for Dedicated GPU Pool — initial questions

Hi Rishi / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — CloudScale is very interested in the Dedicated offering. Before we get procurement involved, can you share more specifics on the throughput guarantees you offer for a reserved commit? In particular:

- How do you define tokens/sec vs requests/sec for the SLA?
- What latency targets (p50/p95) do you guarantee for generator workloads at steady-state?
- What's your measurement methodology (test harness, warm-up, cache policy) so we know what "meeting the SLA" means?

We're considering a 12-month reserved commit but need confidence about steady-state performance for our LLM-based analytics pipeline (mostly single-turn generation and batching of prompts). Also curious how discount tiers map to guaranteed throughput (e.g., how many tokens/sec come with a 500k token/day commit).

Can you send a short, concrete matrix and a proposed verification plan we can include in our SOW?

Best,
Nina
Nina Torres
Head of Platform Engineering
CloudScale Analytics

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Nina Torres <nina@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing/SLAs for Dedicated GPU Pool — initial questions

Nina — thanks for the clear list. I pulled in Laura (pricing) and Monica (SRE) so we can give precise answers and a reproducible test plan. High level answers up front:

- SLA metrics: we publish both sustained tokens/sec (token emission rate) and requests/sec (inference request throughput) as part of Dedicated SLAs. They map to the GPU pool size and the model profile.
- Latency: we target p50/p95 numbers per model class; we can commit to p95 ceilings tied to a given config.
- Measurement: we require a warm-up period, a defined steady-state window, and a recorded test harness run (we share tooling).

Laura will attach a proposed pricing matrix and a draft measurement plan. If those look good we can lock numbers in the contract and schedule a canary validation run.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Nina Torres <nina@cloudscale.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing/SLAs for Dedicated GPU Pool — initial questions

Hi Nina — attaching a short pricing/throughput matrix (see attachment stub). Key points:

- Commit tiers: 3/6/12 month reserved commits. Discounts step with commit size; typical enterprise tiering shown in the XLS.
- Baseline guarantees (example, model class: Llama-2-70B-Chat / 8xA100 equivalent pool):
  * Guaranteed sustained throughput: 22,000 tokens/sec per 8x-A100 pool (measured net emission across all workers)
  * Request throughput: up to 850 requests/sec (1-shot average payload)
  * Latency ceilings: p50 <= 400ms, p95 <= 1.8s for stated request size (single prompt ~256 tokens in, up to 512 tokens out)
- Overage and burst: committed capacity covers steady-state; bursts above commit are allowed via burst buffer at higher per-token rate.

Measurement highlights in the XLS and attached test-plan:
- Warm-up: 5 minutes of progressive ramp to prime KV cache and model kernels
- Steady-state window: 10 continuous minutes; tokens/sec measured as the average token emission rate across that window (excluding ramp)
- Request definition: a single inference call that may produce multiple tokens; requests/sec measured at the API layer before tokenization
- Reproducibility: we run 3 runs and report the median steady-state value; customer and Redwood jointly validate in a canary run before going live

I've attached "proposed_commit_pricing_v2.xlsx" (pricing matrix) and included "throughput-test-plan.md" as the measurement doc. If you want tighter latency ceilings we can discuss a higher commit or a dedicated low-latency tier.

Next steps: can you confirm target model(s) and an initial commit size (ballpark), and we will turn this into an SOW section with explicit numbers and test criteria?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Commercial Pricing
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_commit_pricing_v2.xlsx (XLSX) — pricing tiers and example mappings

Subject: Re: Sizing/SLAs for Dedicated GPU Pool — initial questions

Hi Laura / Rishi,

Thanks for the detailed matrix. A few clarification questions from procurement before we loop legal:

1) Measurement specifics: you state a 5-minute warm-up and a 10-minute steady-state window. Does the warm-up have to be run on our production data (which includes long prefix caching), or can we use replayed/synthetic prompt streams? What does Redwood consider a "warm cache"?

2) SLA measurement artifact: what exact logs/artifacts will Redwood produce to demonstrate a pass/fail? We usually require CSVs with per-second tokens/sec, per-request latency distributions, and the raw harness config.

3) Credits: if you miss the committed tokens/sec or p95 ceiling, what is the credit formula? We would like to propose a 10% service credit for a single failing canary run and tiered credits for repeated misses.

4) Pricing: given our expected profile (avg day: 600k tokens/day; spikes to 2M tokens/day), we'd like to see a discount structure that gives us at least a 20% net reduction vs pay-as-you-go for a 12-month commit.

We can take an internal review today; if you can confirm the measurement artifacts and the exact credit mechanics, we can schedule a final commercial call.

Regards,
Anya Patel
Senior Manager, Procurement
CloudScale Analytics

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Patel <procurement@cloudscale.com>, Nina Torres <nina@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing/SLAs for Dedicated GPU Pool — initial questions

Anya / Nina — addressing each of your procurement bullets and proposing a concrete verification plan you can bake into the SOW:

1) Warm-up / cache policy
- Acceptable inputs: we support both replayed/synthetic streams and production traffic for the warm-up phase. We define "warm cache" as: KV cache hit rate >= 85% for the workload profile and model kernel caches populated (no major JIT recompiles) for the active sequence lengths. We provide a simple cache-priming script to run against a customer's dataset.

2) SLA measurement artifacts
- Redwood will provide the following artifacts for canary/validation runs:
  * per-second CSV of tokens_emitted, requests_started, requests_completed
  * per-request latency (ms) with timestamp and request id (CSV)
  * harness config (concurrency, prompt file, model, max_new_tokens) and Docker image+tag used
  * aggregated report: steady-state avg tokens/sec, max observed requests/sec, p50/p95 latency
- These are produced by our internal bench; we share the raw CSVs and a signed verification summary.

3) Credit mechanics
- Proposal: single missed canary run -> 10% one-time credit applied to next invoice; repeated failures (2/quarter) -> 20% credit and escalation; systemic miss (3 consecutive failures) -> termination rights + pro-rated refund. We'll put exact thresholds in the SOW.

4) Pricing / discount
- We can get to your 20% target on a 12-month commit at the volumes you indicated (600k avg / 2M spikes) by sizing the commit at the 80th percentile daily usage and adding a modest overcommit buffer. Laura's XLS shows a scenario (12-month / commit band C) that hits ~22% discount vs pay-as-you-go. Final numbers will be in an addendum.

Measurement methodology (concrete):
- Model & config: Llama-2-70B-chat equivalent; prompt profile: avg in 220 tokens, max_out 512 tokens
- Warm-up: 5 minute ramp (0 -> target concurrency), then 5 minutes steady priming to reach KV hit rate target
- Steady-state: 10 minute window used to compute the SLA metrics. We take the median of 3 runs for acceptance.
- Tokens/sec definition: mean token emission per second across the steady-state window across all workers; requests/sec: number of inference requests accepted by API layer per second
- Latency: p95 measured on request completion time (end-to-end, including token emission) across steady-state window

Operational next steps:
- If you confirm the above, we will:
  1) Draft the SLA section for the SOW with the exact commit numbers and credit table
  2) Schedule a 2-hour canary window with Redwood SRE + CloudScale ops (we'll provide the harness and guide you through a joint run)
  3) After successful validation, sign the SOW and begin capacity provisioning (lead time ~3 weeks)

I've uploaded the test plan artifact (throughput-test-plan.md) and will circulate the SOW draft after you confirm the model and approximate commit band.

Would you like to book the canary window next week? I'm available Tue/Wed (US/PST).

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
Attachment: throughput-test-plan.md (Markdown) — instruments + CSV schema for SLA validation
